sections.label: THINKING
sections.content:
Interesting! After SPACE with white on the current state (white 65px + purple 25px + white 10px), I got single white 65px. So SPACE with white merged everything to white, but only 65px (not 90px or 100px).
Then SPACE with purple from [24,25] on single white 65px gave:
- id=13: purple 65px at [34,27]-[43,36] (purple on top)
- id=14: white 15px at [39,32]-[43,36] (white in bottom-right)
- id=15: white 10px at [40,28]-[43,31] (white in bottom-left)
- id=16: purple 10px at [40,32]-[43,35] (purple in bottom-right, inside white area)
So this is purple-over-white, but with a complex pattern in the bottom. Total: 65 + 15 + 10 + 10 = 100px. Purple: 65 + 10 = 75px. White: 15 + 10 = 25px.
Then SPACE with purple from [24,25] on this state gave the same result (idempotent).
So the pattern is:
- SPACE with white → single white 65px (regardless of input state)
- SPACE with purple from [24,25] on single white 65px → purple 75px + white 25px (complex pattern)
- SPACE with purple from [24,25] on purple 75px + white 25px → same (idempotent)
The goal is white 50px + purple 50px (clean horizontal split). I'm getting purple 75px + white 25px (complex pattern).
I need to find a way to get white 50px + purple 50px.
Let me try SPACE with purple from different frame positions on single white 65px.
Actually, let me reconsider. The goal panel shows white on top, purple on bottom. The current state shows purple on top, white on bottom (with a complex pattern). What if I need to flip the colors?
What if SPACE with white from some frame position on the current purple-over-white state gives white-over-purple?
Let me try SPACE with white from [21,14] on the current state.

            print(f"  id={n['id']:2d} color={n['color']:2s} px={n['pixels']:4d} rect=[{rmin},{cmin}]-[{rmax},{cmax}]")
print("Level completed:", result.get('level_completed'))
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
